title: Fleet autoscaler: enforce customer min/max bounds + structured decision logs
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Summary: This changes the Dedicated fleet autoscaler control loop to enforce customer-configured hard bounds (min/max replicas) on every reconcile, and emits structured decision logs describing inputs, intermediate desired replicas, clamp reasons, and the applied actuation. Includes integration tests that validate: (1) no bound violations, (2) correct clamp reasons, and (3) no-op behavior when bounds are unset/legacy. Context: Customers have repeatedly asked for strict spend controls (max) and predictable baseline capacity (min). Prior behavior could overshoot during spikes (especially when backlog-based scaling kicked in) and logs were too ad-hoc to explain why we scaled. This PR is the autoscaler-side piece; control plane schema + policy evaluation output are handled in ENG-2841/ENG-2842. Behavior changes: - The autoscaler now treats bounds as hard limits: desired_replicas is computed as before, then clamped to [min_replicas, max_replicas] if present in evaluated config. - If the computed desired exceeds max, we clamp and record clamp_reason=MAX_BOUND. If below min, clamp_reason=MIN_BOUND. If within bounds, clamp_reason=NONE. - When bounds are missing (legacy pools), no clamping occurs and clamp_reason=UNBOUNDED. - If config is invalid (should not happen post-policy-eval), we fail closed to a safe behavior: treat as unbounded but emit clamp_reason=INVALID_CONFIG and include validation_errors in the log payload. (This is defensive; control plane validation should prevent it.) - Decision logs are emitted once per reconcile per pool (rate-limited) and use the standard structured logging interface so downstream can attach to audit trail work (ENG-2847). Logging: A new structured event `autoscaler.scaling_decision.v1` is emitted with fields: pool_id, region, hw_class, current_replicas, reactive_desired_replicas, predicted_desired_replicas (nullable), chosen_desired_replicas_pre_clamp, chosen_desired_replicas_post_clamp, min_replicas, max_replicas, clamp_reason, scale_action (UP/DOWN/NOOP), cooldown_blocked (bool), and primary_signals (compact string; no high-cardinality arrays). NOTE: This PR does not add metrics; it adds logs. Metrics/dashboards are in ENG-2846 / observability-pack#842. Tests: - Added integration tests for the reconcile loop using the fake fleet actuator + seeded signal inputs. Scenarios include: clamp-at-max during spike, clamp-at-min after demand drop, and legacy no-bounds config. - Tests also ensure clamp is applied after reactive calculation but before cooldown/scale-rate limiting is evaluated (see reviewer notes below); this preserves the invariant that the controller never attempts actuation outside bounds. Rollout notes: The clamping behavior is behind the existing Dedicated autoscaling controller; the customer-exposed feature flag/allowlist is handled separately (ENG-2848). This PR is safe to ship as it is no-op until evaluated bounds are present in config. Follow-ups: - Predictive blending and confidence gating will add predicted_desired_replicas and alter how chosen_desired_replicas_pre_clamp is computed (ENG-2845). This PR intentionally keeps the clamping layer independent so we have a single point of enforcement. - We should confirm cardinality guardrails once Console audit trail starts consuming these logs (ENG-2847).
commits: autoscaler: clamp desired replicas to evaluated min/max bounds
autoscaler: emit autoscaler.scaling_decision.v1 structured log event
tests: integration tests for bounded scaling scenarios
refactor: extract clamp logic into ScalingBounds helper + unit tests
review_conversation: Vanessa Ortiz: Please confirm clamping happens before we attempt to compute scale deltas / rate limits. If we clamp after rate limits, we can still emit intent > max in logs and confuse customers. Keiko Yamamoto (author): Good catch. I moved clamping to occur immediately after computing chosen_desired_replicas_pre_clamp and before any cooldown/scale-rate limiting. Updated tests to assert the logged post_clamp value is always within bounds, even when cooldown prevents actuation. Jamal Pierce: What is the behavior when max is set above our regional supply? Do we risk repeatedly trying to scale up and failing? Keiko Yamamoto: This PR doesn’t change supply constraints handling: actuation may fail due to capacity; we now log the chosen desire (post-clamp) and the actuator response. A separate PR will add a distinct `actuation_result=CAPACITY_CONSTRAINED` reason once the actuator plumbs it through (tracked in ENG-2843 follow-up). Rafael Mendes: SRE concern: log payload could get big / high cardinality. Can we avoid dumping raw signals? Keiko Yamamoto: Agreed. I kept `primary_signals` as a compact string enum-ish summary (e.g., "queue_depth+p95_latency") and removed any raw arrays. We only include pool_id/region/hw_class and the numeric desired values. Allison Grant: Naming: clamp_reason should be stable and documented. Also please version the event name. Keiko Yamamoto: Updated to `autoscaler.scaling_decision.v1` and clamp_reason is an enum with: NONE, UNBOUNDED, MIN_BOUND, MAX_BOUND, INVALID_CONFIG. Jordan Lee: Minor: if config is invalid, "fail closed" should likely mean no scale rather than unbounded. Keiko Yamamoto: We debated this. Since policy eval should guarantee validity, INVALID_CONFIG is an emergency-only path. Current behavior keeps the system available and relies on alerting + operator intervention; scaling will still be constrained by other guardrails (cooldown/scale-rate limits). Happy to change if we prefer "NOOP"; added a TODO with a pointer to ADR-0142 discussion for final call. Vanessa Ortiz: Approved after the clamp ordering fix + integration tests. Rafael Mendes: Approved; please ensure we add an alert for INVALID_CONFIG occurrences when metrics land. Keiko Yamamoto: Ack; added to ENG-2846 checklist.
merge_outcome: Merged to main via squash; deployed to staging automatically. Production rollout gated by allowlist/feature flag work in ENG-2848.
